note: Candidate statements document HTTP 400 for specific endpoints when input is invalid, but do not document the global Web API exception handler behavior mapping any IllegalArgumentException to HTTP 400.
Web API response mapping HTTP 500 for IllegalStateException is not documented.
Endpoints individually document HTTP 404 when referenced entities are not found, but a general exception mapping rule for ObjectUnknownException across the Web API is not explicitly stated.
Endpoint specs (including POST /transportOrders/{NAME}) confirm that when an object already exists in the model (ObjectExistsException), the API returns HTTP 409.
Web API response mapping HTTP 500 for KernelRuntimeException is not documented.
Code states property value is optional, whereas OpenAPI schema specifies Property.value as required ('common:Property.value; required; type string.').
Documentation confirms that a transport order destination is defined by the destination location name and an operation, with optional properties.
Transport order schema confirms destinations is required, while incompleteName, dispensable, deadline, dependencies, and other fields are optional.
DestinationState describing a drive order destination by its location name, operation, properties list, and execution state is not fully covered in candidates.

Code specifies destination state can be PRISTINE, TRAVELLING, OPERATING, FINISHED, FAILED; documentation includes ACTIVE in DestinationState ('PRISTINE, ACTIVE, TRAVELLING, OPERATING, FINISHED, FAILED').
Transport order OpenAPI spec confirms Route contains required costs (int64) and required steps array.
Full RouteStep schema including sourcePoint, destinationPoint, path, vehicleOrientation, routeIndex, costs, executionAllowed, and reroutingType is not fully covered across the candidates.

TransportOrderState response schema in transport-orders.yaml documents all transport order fields.
TransportOrderState.state in transport-orders.yaml documents RAW, ACTIVE, DISPATCHABLE, BEING_PROCESSED, WITHDRAWN, FINISHED, FAILED, UNROUTABLE.
POST /transportOrders/dispatcher/trigger is documented to trigger kernel dispatching and return 200 OK.
Endpoint POST /transportOrders/{NAME}/immediateAssignment is documented to immediately assign the transport order to its intended vehicle.
HTTP 404 response when the transport order name does not exist is not documented in OpenAPI/Web API docs for immediateAssignment.
Endpoint POST /transportOrders/{NAME}/withdrawal withdraws the transport order with the given name.
HTTP 404 response when no transport order exists with NAME on POST /transportOrders/{NAME}/withdrawal is undocumented in the Web API spec.
Documented query parameter 'immediate' with default false, controlling whether the transport order is aborted as quickly as possible.
Query parameter 'disableVehicle' is documented for withdrawal; behavior updates vehicle integration level to TO_BE_RESPECTED (documented as deprecated in favor of setting integration level directly).
POST /transportOrders/{NAME} creates a new transport order with the given name and request body details, returning created order details.
HTTP 400 Bad Request error for malformed JSON request body on POST /transportOrders/{NAME} is not explicitly documented.
Default transport order type '-' when omitted is not documented in the Web API specifications.
Returning HTTP 404 when a destination refers to a nonexistent point/location is not documented for POST /transportOrders/{NAME}.
Returning HTTP 400 when point destination specifies an operation other than MOVE or PARK is not documented.

None of the candidates document that the web API returns HTTP status 400 Bad Request when a location destination specifies an operation not permitted by the location type and at least one attached link (or NOP).
Changelog mentions allowing types, but the web API rejection with HTTP 400 Bad Request when adding an order with mismatched type to a wrapping sequence is not documented in the API docs.
Statement D-0912 specifies PUT /transportOrders/{NAME}/intendedVehicle updates the transport order's intended vehicle.
Statement D-0914 documents the query parameter 'vehicle' as optional for PUT /transportOrders/{NAME}/intendedVehicle to assign the vehicle.
None of the candidates document the HTTP 404 response when the transport order specified by NAME does not exist for PUT intendedVehicle.
No statement documents HTTP 404 when the vehicle specified in the vehicle query parameter does not exist.
No candidate statement covers HTTP 400 being returned when updating intendedVehicle if the transport order is not in RAW, ACTIVE, or DISPATCHABLE state.
Statement D-0891 documents GET /transportOrders/{NAME} using the NAME path parameter to retrieve the transport order.
None of the candidate statements document the HTTP 404 response when retrieving a transport order that does not exist.
The sorting of returned transport orders ascending by name on GET /transportOrders is not documented in the candidate statements.
Statement D-0887 specifies GET /transportOrders with optional query parameter intendedVehicle to filter retrieved transport orders by the intended vehicle.
No candidate statement documents that GET /transportOrders returns HTTP 404 if the vehicle specified by intendedVehicle does not exist.
